Hindi इम्तहान Borrowed from Classical Persian اِمْتِحَان (imtihān), borrowed from Arabic اِمْتِحَان (imtiḥān), from اِمْتَحَنَ (imtaḥana). First attested in c. 1611 as Middle Hindi امتحان (amtḥan /⁠imtihān⁠/).
Sanskritic formation from ऐच्छिक (aicchik, “voluntary”) + मांसपेशी (mānspeśī, “muscle”); calque of English voluntary muscle. Sometimes also shortened and written as ऐच्छिक पेशी (aicchik peśī).
Borrowed from Classical Persian کار (kār), from Middle Persian kʾl (kār). Compare with Sanskrit कार (kāra, “tax”).
Borrowed from Sanskrit कार (kāra), from कृ (kṛ). Alternatively also from 'Etymology 1'.
